title: The Repair Shop on Maple Street · 独立口语迁移
instructions: 先完成示范段的跟读诊断，再用不同人物、信息或立场录制自己的完整回答。示范与自由回答分别取证，服务未提供完整听音评阅时保持待评。
reference: When the Maple Street Repair Shop opened in 2019, it had one workbench, two volunteers, and a simple rule: fix first, replace last. The shop occupies a former garage in the centre of town. People bring in broken lamps, torn coats, and old radios, and volunteers try to repair them free of charge. If a repair is impossible, the item is sent to a recycling centre rather than thrown away. The shop's growth has been striking. In its first year, it repaired 312 items; by 2023, that figure had reached 1,140. Over the same period, the number of volunteers rose from two to nineteen, most of them retired engineers or hobbyists. The shop does not sell new products. It only repairs what people already own, which keeps costs low and waste lower still. This focus on repair rather than replacement is central to its environmental aims. Maya Chen, the shop's coordinator, says the growth was never planned.
